tasks.short: Report the month's figures to the directors.

today.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract has landed and the close calendar says the management pack is due.
steps: Export the trial balance and the three site results from AFAS Profit.
Rebuild Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo in Excel and reconcile the totals to Power BI.
Split own staff, flex labour, warehouse and transport against the FP&A forecast.
Write a short note on the variances that will raise questions.
Send the pack and walk the Finance Director and the site leads through it.
drudgery: Rebuilding the same workbook after every nightly refresh.
Hunting differences between the Excel pack and Power BI.
Reformatting tables and carrying forward last month's sentences.
today.time_sinks: Most of the time goes into copying figures and making the three site views agree, before anyone reads the story.

lenses.faster: Once the period is locked the pack is filled from the extract, so the export, the site split and the tie to Power BI leave the accountant's morning. What remains is reading the variances and the meeting with the directors.
lenses.autonomous: A locked period in AFAS starts the pack on its own. A failed tie waits for the accountant; a clean pack waits for approval before it is mailed.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the cost the directors would want this every week, by site and by lane, with the same flex-labour bridge the forecast already uses.
lenses.joy: The copy-paste and the format repairs go. Explaining a real movement to the person who runs a warehouse stays.
lenses.options: The same locked numbers can carry a one-page note for the Finance Director, a page per site, and a short list of questions for FP&A.
lenses.altitude: The accountant sets the line definitions, the variance thresholds and the sign-off rule, and reviews the pack the job produced.
reach: FP&A analyst: first draft of the bridge from actuals to the forecast
Controller: the monthly commentary that now waits on a fresh Excel file
Bookkeeper: the cost-centre mismatches that keep breaking the site view

tasks.human_edge: Judging which variance a site lead will challenge, and whether a flex-labour spike is the season, a late agency invoice or a wrong cost centre.
tasks.pattern_why: The figures come from a structured ledger, but the pack is something the business is asked to trust, so it counts only after an accountant has accepted the variances and the wording.

in_practice.trigger: AFAS period lock for the month, after the nightly extract.
steps: Pull the locked trial balance, the three site cost centres and the FP&A forecast into the pack.
Tie every total to Power BI and to the general ledger, and list anything that fails.
Draft the variance notes for own staff, flex labour, warehouse and transport.
Place the pack in the SharePoint close library for the accountant.
in_practice.human_gate: One accountant approves the pack before it goes to the Finance Director. The director decides what the sites are told.
data_needed: Locked trial balance by site and cost centre
FP&A forecast on the same categories
Prior month pack and open items
Flex-labour cost from agency invoices posted in AFAS
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint close library, with the ledger period, the extract time and the name of the approver.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit and Power BI already produce ledger-based statements and dashboards, so a site pack does not have to be retyped.
A language model can draft variance commentary from a stable table of categories.
Commentary that management will use for a forecast needs a person who can tell a late agency invoice from a real movement.

risks: A fluent note can hide a late agency invoice or a bad cost-centre map, and the sites then trust a weak forecast.
The Power BI extract is nightly, so a morning pack can miss journals posted after the refresh.
Labour-cost labels differ between the transport CAO and the warehouse CAO, so one template can mis-state a site.
A note that drills to a named employee pulls personal data into the draft and is unnecessary for a site pack.
research_questions: After the ledger is locked, how many hours does the pack take, and how many of those are tying Excel to Power BI?
In the last six closes, how often was a variance in the pack later reversed?
Will the Finance Director accept wording an accountant has signed, or do they expect the accountant's own sentences?
Are site cost centres and flex-labour accounts stable enough to map without a manual bridge?

tasks.short: Calculate VAT and corporate tax and file the returns.

today.trigger: The VAT period is ending, or the controller asks for the corporate-tax provision before the month locks.
steps: Run the AFAS VAT overview and compare it with the sales and purchase ledgers.
Clear mismatched VAT codes on agency invoices, carrier invoices and credit notes with the bookkeepers.
Check cross-border transport and warehouse services for the right Dutch VAT treatment.
Build the corporate-tax provision from the result before tax and the standing differences.
File the VAT return, release the Rabobank payment, and send the annual corporate-tax file to the external advisor.
drudgery: Ticking VAT boxes back to piles of invoices.
Chasing the same wrong VAT code on agency and carrier invoices each period.
Rebuilding the corporate-tax bridge in Excel every month.
today.time_sinks: Once AFAS holds the VAT codes, the hours sit in exceptions and in rebuilding the tax bridge, more than in the arithmetic.

lenses.faster: The VAT boxes and the corporate-tax bridge fill from the ledger when the period closes. The accountant opens only the lines the rules cannot place.
lenses.autonomous: Period close starts the VAT draft and the tax bridge. A mismatch above a set amount waits; a clean draft still waits for approval before anyone files.
lenses.ambitious: Done properly means every agency and carrier invoice carries a VAT code that would survive a Belastingdienst check, and the provision moves with the result during the month.
lenses.joy: The box-ticking goes. The odd transport job, and the decision to file a suppletie, stay.
lenses.options: Show the return on current codes, on a corrected coding of the open mismatches, and with the suppletie in this period or the next.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the VAT decision table and the tax-bridge rules, and reviews the lines that fall outside them.
reach: Bookkeeper: VAT coding on purchase invoices before they are posted
Payroll specialist: tying the wage-tax position in the ledger to the payroll declaration
Controller: the tax line in the monthly pack

tasks.human_edge: Deciding the VAT treatment of a transport leg that has no standard code, and whether a found error is large enough to file a suppletie now.
tasks.pattern_why: The VAT arithmetic is rules on coded invoices, but filing with the Belastingdienst is a legal act and the open items are real exceptions, so a person approves every return.

in_practice.trigger: The AFAS VAT period closes, or the close checklist reaches the corporate-tax provision.
steps: Build the VAT boxes from the AFAS codes and list every line with a missing or unusual code.
Match agency and carrier invoices to the posted VAT and flag differences.
Roll the result before tax into the corporate-tax bridge with the standing permanent differences.
Prepare the VAT payment amount for the Rabobank batch.
Leave the draft return and the bridge for approval.
in_practice.human_gate: An accountant approves the VAT return before it is filed and before the Rabobank payment is released. The annual corporate-tax return still goes through the external tax advisor.
data_needed: VAT codes on sales and purchase invoices
Agency and carrier invoices for the period
Result before tax and the standing tax adjustments
The prior return and open suppleties
in_practice.logs_to: The AFAS tax dossier and the SharePoint tax folder, with the period, the filing reference and the approver.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit can prepare a Dutch VAT return from VAT codes on the ledger and supports electronic filing.
The annual Dutch corporate-tax return is commonly prepared in specialist tax software or by an external advisor from a bridge the company supplies.
Place of supply, and the zero rate on some international transport, are frequent VAT error points in logistics.

risks: A wrong filed return draws interest, a penalty or a Belastingdienst review of several years.
Inlenersaansprakelijkheid on flex labour is invisible in a VAT code: a clean return can still sit on invoices from a non-compliant agency.
If an uncoded invoice receives an invented VAT treatment, the ledger and the return drift apart.
research_questions: In the last four VAT periods, what share of purchase invoices had the VAT code changed after posting?
Does AFAS already produce the return that is filed, and how many manual adjustments does that draft need?
Who files the corporate-tax return today, this team or an external advisor, and which part is still an Excel bridge?
How many transport invoices sit outside the standard Dutch 21 percent treatment?

tasks.short: Review assets, liabilities and the result before close.

today.trigger: The close checklist reaches the balance-sheet review, in the first week after month end.
steps: Export the trial balance and the fixed-asset, debtor, creditor and bank subledgers from AFAS.
Tie each balance to the general ledger and the Rabobank statement.
Recalculate the holiday-pay accrual, the flex-labour accrual, leases and prepayments.
Look for a site or an account that moved without a known cause.
Write what the controller must clear before the period locks.
drudgery: Ticking subledgers to the general ledger by hand.
Rebuilding holiday-pay and flex accruals that follow the same CAO rules every month.
Copying last month's review notes into a new workbook.
today.time_sinks: The tie-out and the accrual rebuild take the time. The judgment is a short list of balances that tie and still look wrong.

lenses.faster: Ties to the subledgers and the bank, and the standard holiday-pay and flex accruals, run when the extract lands. The accountant reviews the breaks.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly extract on the first close day starts the review. A balance that ties and sits inside its threshold needs no reminder.
lenses.ambitious: The company would check every material balance every week, on one holiday-pay rule and one lease schedule shared by all three sites.
lenses.joy: The ticking goes. Finding the accrual that is actually wrong, before the auditor does, stays.
lenses.options: For each break, show the balance as posted, the balance after the proposed correction, and the effect on the site result and the forecast.
lenses.altitude: The accountant sets the tie-out rules, the thresholds and the accrual formulas, and changes them when the same break keeps returning.
reach: Bookkeeper: debtor and creditor differences that fail the tie-out
FP&A analyst: the working-capital balances the forecast depends on
Payroll specialist: holiday pay, unused leave and shift-premium accruals under both CAOs

tasks.human_edge: Seeing that a balance ties and is still wrong, such as a Venlo goods cutoff on the last Friday or a flex accrual that still uses last month's hours.
tasks.pattern_why: The ties and the standard accruals are rules with a checkable result. A balance enters the locked period only after a person has accepted the exceptions.

in_practice.trigger: The nightly AFAS extract on the first close day, and again when the bookkeepers mark the subledgers ready.
steps: Tie fixed assets, debtors, creditors and the Rabobank balance to the general ledger.
Recalculate holiday pay, unused leave and the flex-labour accrual from the standing CAO rules.
Flag balances that moved beyond the threshold or that failed the tie.
Draft the correction for each break and park it for approval.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant clears every break before the period locks. A clean balance is covered by the close checklist.
data_needed: Trial balance and subledgers
Rabobank statement
Headcount, wage rates and the two CAO accrual rules
Open agency invoices and goods received not invoiced
Lease and asset register
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint close checklist, one line per account, with the tie result and the person who cleared a break.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit keeps debtor, creditor, bank and fixed-asset subledgers that are built to agree to the general ledger.
Close tools such as BlackLine match accounts, route breaks and record who cleared them.

Dutch holiday pay is a set percentage of eligible wage plus unused leave, so the monthly accrual can be recalculated from payroll totals, with different rules for the transport CAO, the warehouse CAO and flex workers.

risks: A wide threshold hides a cutoff error at one site. A tight threshold trains people to accept breaks without reading them.
Holiday pay and shift premiums differ between the two CAOs, and flex workers accrue on the agency invoice, so one formula will mis-state a site.
An accrual that posts on its own can put a wrong result into the forecast.
research_questions: How many balance-sheet accounts are still tied in Excel, and how many fail in a normal month?
Are holiday pay, leave and flex accruals calculated in AFAS today, or in one accountant's workbook?
What share of last year's audit adjustments sat in accounts this review is meant to catch?
Does the Rabobank import match the AFAS bank ledger line for line?

tasks.short: Write the report on what the audit found.

today.trigger: A piece of internal testing finishes, or the external auditor sends findings and asks for a reply.
steps: Collect the samples, the exceptions and the explanations from the bookkeepers and from payroll.
Decide which exceptions are findings and how serious they are.
Write the condition, the cause, the amount and the proposed action.
Have the controller read it before it goes to the Finance Director or back to the auditor.
Store the evidence in the audit folder on SharePoint.
drudgery: Reformatting the same finding into the auditor's template.
Chasing an invoice that was already attached to the AFAS booking.
Keeping versions of the reply straight across mailboxes.
today.time_sinks: Rewriting each finding for a different reader takes as long as deciding whether it is a finding.

lenses.faster: The first draft of each finding is written from the exception list and the evidence already on the booking, in the structure the auditor asked for. The accountant edits the severity and the action.
lenses.autonomous: A completed test that has exceptions opens a draft finding. A clean test logs a clean result and does not sit in a reminder list.
lenses.ambitious: Every recurring break would be written up in the month it happens, so the year-end letter is short and the same point is not discovered twice.
lenses.joy: The reformatting goes. Pinning down the real cause with the bookkeeper who posted it stays.
lenses.options: From the same facts, draft a management-letter point, a close defect, and a process remark that stays inside the team.
lenses.altitude: The accountant keeps the finding catalogue and the severity rules, and checks that new drafts match how the team speaks to the auditor.
reach: Controller: the first draft of the management-letter reply
Bookkeeper: the evidence pack on an invoice sample
Payroll specialist: findings on wage cost, allowances and CAO premiums

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what is a real finding, and which wording should reach the external auditor only with the controller's context.
tasks.pattern_why: A finding changes what management and the auditor believe about the books. The draft can be assembled from the test, and it counts only after the accountant and the controller agree the wording.

in_practice.trigger: A control test is marked complete, or an external finding arrives by mail.
steps: Pull the exceptions, the amounts and the attachments already stored on the AFAS booking or in SharePoint.
Draft each finding with the condition, the cause, the amount and a proposed action.
Match the draft to open findings so the same point is not written twice.
Route the draft to the accountant with the evidence linked.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant signs the draft. The controller signs anything that leaves the team, including replies to the external auditor.
data_needed: Test results and sample exceptions
Supporting documents already on the booking
Open findings and the prior management letter
The auditor's template
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint audit library, with the version, the draft author and both approvers.

evidence.claim: DataSnipper pulls audit evidence from source documents into Excel workpapers and is used by audit firms.
CaseWare documents audit work and findings in a set structure.
An external auditor re-performs the work that supports the opinion and treats a client's narrative as input.

risks: A polished draft can overstate a finding, and that sentence is hard to walk back once the auditor has copied it.
An evidence link that points at the wrong invoice creates a file that looks complete.
Employee names in a payroll sample are personal data under the AVG and do not belong in a finding that is mailed widely.
research_questions: How many findings last year repeated a point already known at a monthly close?
Does the external auditor accept drafts in their template, or do they rewrite them in their own file?
Where does the evidence live today: on the AFAS booking, in SharePoint, or in a mailbox?
Of the hours on a finding, how many go to formatting and how many to deciding severity?

tasks.short: Work out leases, discounts and depreciation for tax and the books.

today.trigger: A warehouse or truck lease is signed or renewed, an asset is capitalised, or the tax bridge needs the depreciation difference.
steps: Read the contract and open the asset card in AFAS.
Set the term, the discount rate and the residual value in a workbook.
Calculate commercial depreciation and the fiscal depreciation allowed for corporate tax.
Propose the monthly journal and the tax difference.
Keep the workbook so the auditor can follow it next year.
drudgery: Adding one truck as a new row in a long spreadsheet.
Copying dates and amounts out of contract PDFs on SharePoint.
Reconciling the workbook total to the AFAS asset subledger.
today.time_sinks: Maintaining the schedules and tying them back to AFAS takes longer than choosing the rate. Bonds, annuities and depletable assets do not arise on these books.

lenses.faster: A new truck, a racking line or a site lease extends the schedule and refreshes the tax difference. The accountant sets the term and the rate.
lenses.autonomous: A new asset card, or a contract saved in the SharePoint contract library, starts a draft schedule. The monthly run for contracts that already have an approved rate needs no reminder.
lenses.ambitious: For every warehouse and every truck the company would see the cost of extending a year, the cost of replacing, and the tax effect in the same view.
lenses.joy: The row-copying goes. The argument about the Venlo lease term, and about whether a rebuild is an asset or a repair, stays.
lenses.options: For each new lease, show a short term, the contract term and a renewal, with the cost, the liability and the fiscal depreciation beside each other.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the rate policy, the useful lives and the check that AFAS and the tax bridge still agree.
reach: FP&A analyst: lease-versus-buy on trucks and warehouse space
Controller: the technical memo the auditor asks for
Bookkeeper: the monthly lease and depreciation journal

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the lease term and the discount rate the auditor will accept, including whether a renewal at Tilburg or Venlo is reasonably certain.
tasks.pattern_why: Once the term, the rate and the life are set, the schedule, the depreciation and the fiscal difference are arithmetic that can tie to AFAS. The run itself does not need a language model. Stocks, bonds, annuities and depletable assets are absent here.

in_practice.trigger: A contract is added to the SharePoint contract library, an asset card is created in AFAS, or the monthly close starts.
steps: Read the term, the payment and the asset from the contract and the AFAS card.
Apply the approved rate and useful life, and flag any contract that has neither.
Calculate the commercial charge, the liability and the fiscal depreciation difference.
Compare the total with the AFAS asset and lease balances.
Prepare the journal for the accountant to post.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves the rate, the term and the useful life for each new or changed contract. Known contracts then run on those inputs, and the accountant posts the journal.
data_needed: Lease contracts and amendments
Asset register with cost, life and method
Approved discount rate and the fiscal depreciation rules
General-ledger balances for leases and depreciation
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint lease file, with the inputs, the schedule version and the approver, plus the journal number in AFAS.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit has a fixed-asset module that calculates depreciation from cost, life and method and can post it to the ledger.
Lease-accounting products such as Visual Lease and Trullion calculate schedules from contract term, payment and discount rate.
Under Dutch GAAP, balance-sheet treatment of a lease and the fiscal depreciation rate still depend on the contract and on Belastingdienst life tables.

risks: A wrong term on the largest warehouse lease moves both the monthly result and the corporate-tax provision.
Fiscal depreciation copied from the commercial schedule is wrong where the allowed tax life differs.
A schedule that lives beside AFAS drifts as soon as someone posts a manual journal.
research_questions: How many lease and depreciation schedules sit in Excel, and do they tie to AFAS this month?
Who chooses the discount rate, and did the auditor challenge it last year?
What share of the tax bridge is depreciation differences?
Are the warehouse leases and the truck leases already in the AFAS asset module?

tasks.short: Test the finance systems and recommend better controls.

today.trigger: A close check fails, the auditor writes a system remark, or the quarterly look at AFAS rights and the Rabobank batch is due.
steps: Follow one process in AFAS, from invoice to payment or from journal to the management pack.
Compare user rights with the work the bookkeepers, payroll and the accountants actually do.
Sample bookings and payment batches against the control the process claims to have.
Ask the person who uses the workaround what they do on a busy Friday.
Write the gap and a practical fix for the controller.
drudgery: Exporting user-rights lists and comparing them by hand.
Retesting a control that failed in the same way last quarter.
Rewriting the same recommendation in a fresh document.
today.time_sinks: Gathering rights, samples and screenshots takes longer than deciding what the control should be.

lenses.faster: The rights export, the sample and a first pass against the control list are ready before the review. The accountant still judges whether the control holds on a shift site.
lenses.autonomous: A change in AFAS rights, or the same close break for a third month, opens a review file. The recommendation stays put until the accountant issues it.
lenses.ambitious: The company would keep one living control list for procure-to-pay, the bank batch and the nightly extract, and would repair a weak control in the month it appears.
lenses.joy: The rights spreadsheets and the screenshot hunt go. Designing a control a bookkeeper will actually follow stays.
lenses.options: For each gap, set out an AFAS configuration change, a detective report, and a manual check, each with the effort and the risk that remains.
lenses.altitude: The accountant owns the control catalogue and the test plan, and spends the review time on the gaps the tests keep finding.
reach: Bookkeeper: the invoice approval path and the coding step
Controller: the control section of the audit file
People Analytics and HRIS analyst: quality checks on the AFAS extract that feeds both the HR and the finance dashboards

tasks.human_edge: Knowing whether a control that looks right in AFAS still fails on a Friday shift at Venlo, and whether the proposed fix will be used.
tasks.pattern_why: The accountant stays responsible for the judgment and the recommendation. The preparation of rights, samples and options can be assisted; the conclusion that a control is sound stays with the person.

in_practice.trigger: An AFAS authorisation change, a repeated close break, or the quarterly control review.
steps: Export the relevant rights, workflow steps and a sample of postings and Rabobank batches.
Mark where the sample does not match the control the catalogue describes.
Draft three ways to close the gap, naming what would change in AFAS or in the bank process.
Leave the review file for the accountant with the samples linked.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant writes the recommendation the controller will see. AFAS rights and the Rabobank batch setup change only with the controller and the existing payment approvers.
data_needed: AFAS authorisation and workflow configuration
A sample of invoices, journals and payment batches
Close breaks and prior audit points
The current control catalogue
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint control catalogue, with the test date, the sample and the recommendation the accountant issued.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit stores user rights and workflow steps that can be exported and compared with who posted and who approved.
Whether a control works on a warehouse shift is a judgment from samples and from the people who run the workaround, beyond what a rights export shows.
Payment batches at Dutch banks, including Rabobank, are normally released by a second authorised person, and that step is a control.

risks: A recommendation based on a rights export misses a shared login or a spreadsheet journal that never uses those rights.
A change to the approval path can weaken the two-person release on the Rabobank batch.
A draft that names AFAS menus can sound exact and still be wrong for this tenant.
research_questions: Can this AFAS tenant export rights and workflow history in a form that matches posted journals?
Which close breaks in the last year were control failures, and which were late agency invoices?
Who can change authorisations today, and is that change logged?
Did the last management letter name system controls the team could not evidence?

tasks.short: Prepare and check the statements and the annual report.

today.trigger: Each month close, and once a year the jaarrekening and the management report for the board, the auditor and the KVK.
steps: Take the locked trial balance from AFAS and map it to the statement lines.
Prepare lead schedules for revenue, labour, leases, tax and equity.
Tie the statements to the monthly pack the directors already saw.
Update the notes from last year's wording.
Support the external auditor and, after the opinion and the board's adoption, help file at the KVK.
drudgery: Mapping the trial balance into a statement workbook by hand.
Rolling forward note wording that barely changed.
Retyping figures the monthly pack already contained.
today.time_sinks: The mapping, the lead schedules and the note updates consume the close. The presentation decisions sit with the controller.

lenses.faster: Statement lines, lead schedules and a first draft of the notes that changed come from the locked trial balance. The accountant checks the mapping and the sentences.
lenses.autonomous: Period lock starts the monthly statements. The annual file starts when the controller opens the year-end folder. KVK filing waits for the auditor's opinion and the board.
lenses.ambitious: A monthly set on the same definitions as the jaarrekening would make the year-end a thin update, and the forecast would use those same lines.
lenses.joy: The mapping and the unchanged notes go. The one note that actually moved, and a clean opinion, stay.
lenses.options: Show the result on the current mapping and on the two presentation choices still open, including where flex labour sits.
lenses.altitude: The accountant maintains the mapping from AFAS to the statement lines and the disclosure checklist, and reviews what the draft produced.
reach: Controller: the disclosure checklist and the first reply to an auditor query on the figures
FP&A analyst: a result bridge that uses the same lines as the statutory result
Finance Director: a first draft of the figures section of the management report

tasks.human_edge: Deciding the presentation and the wording the board will sign and the auditor will test, including what the management report claims about the year.
tasks.pattern_why: The statements are a mapping from a locked ledger plus disclosures. They become the company's accounts only after the accountant and the controller approve them, and the Finance Director signs the annual set.

in_practice.trigger: The AFAS period is locked, or the controller opens the year-end file.
steps: Map the locked trial balance to the statement lines with the approved mapping.
Build the lead schedules and flag any line that does not tie to the monthly pack or the ledger.
Draft the notes that changed and carry forward the notes that did not, with the changes marked.
Compare flex labour, leases and tax with the schedules already approved in the close.
Place the pack in the SharePoint year-end library.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant approves the monthly statements. The controller approves the annual statements. The Finance Director signs the management report. Filing at the KVK waits for the auditor.
data_needed: Locked trial balance
Approved mapping to statement lines
Lead schedules from the close
Prior-year signed jaarrekening
Auditor query list
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint reporting library, with the ledger period, the mapping version and each approver.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit produces a trial balance and financial statements from the general ledger.
CaseWare and Silverfin produce statutory accounts and disclosure notes from a trial balance.
A company of this size files the jaarrekening at the KVK in SBR format after the board adopts it, and the statutory audit applies well below 1,200 employees.

risks: A mapping error copied into fluent notes becomes the version the board saw all year.
The management report is a directors' document. A draft that overclaims on the forecast or on controls creates liability for the signatories.
If the monthly pack and the statutory mapping treat flex labour differently, the sites will trust neither figure.
research_questions: Is the statement mapping maintained in AFAS, in a tool such as CaseWare or Silverfin, or in a workbook?
How many notes changed in substance last year, and how many were rolled forward with only the figures updated?
Do the monthly management figures use the same lines as the statutory result?
Who prepares the SBR file for the KVK, and how many days after the opinion is it filed?

tasks.short: Check bookings and talk to staff when they look wrong.

today.trigger: An audit sample, a VAT or cost-centre exception, or a site result the pack cannot explain.
steps: Pull the bookings and the attachments from AFAS.
Pick the sample and note what is missing or coded oddly.
Arrange a short conversation with the warehouse clerk, the planner or the bookkeeper who knows the job.
Write down what they said and whether the booking should change.
Send the correction to the bookkeeper and put it on the close file.
drudgery: Opening booking after booking to find the attachment.
Building the sample list by hand.
Writing up conversations that all started from the same questions.
today.time_sinks: The time splits between pulling records and reaching shift staff who are not at a desk during the close.

lenses.faster: The sample, the missing attachments and a short question list are ready before the conversation. The conversation stays on the accountant's calendar.
lenses.autonomous: A failed tie-out or a VAT exception assembles the file and names the role that is likely to know. It does not contact the employee.
lenses.ambitious: Coding and cutoff questions would be settled with the site in the same week, so the year-end sample is small and the same Venlo cutoff does not return every January.
lenses.joy: The attachment hunt goes. A clerk explaining a real shipment is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: For the same exception, prepare a VAT question list, a cutoff question list and a cost-centre question list, and let the documents decide which one is used.
lenses.altitude: The accountant designs the tests and the questions, watches which exceptions return, and sits down only for the ones the records cannot answer.
reach: Bookkeeper: a vendor-statement difference that needs a phone call
Credit and collections officer: a debtor dispute that is really a missing proof of delivery
Payroll specialist: a wage booking that does not match the CAO allowance

tasks.human_edge: Talking with a clerk on a shift so the question is about the booking, and hearing the explanation that is not in the attachment.
tasks.pattern_why: The record pull and the question list can be prepared. The conversation, the reading of what the person means, and the decision to change a booking stay with the accountant.

in_practice.trigger: A close break, a VAT exception, or an audit sample that the documents do not explain.
steps: Assemble the booking, the invoice, the goods receipt and prior exceptions of the same type.
Draft a short question list aimed at the missing fact.
Name the role that is likely to know, and send nothing to that person.
After the conversation, write up the fact in the accountant's words and propose the correction.
in_practice.human_gate: The accountant decides whether to speak to someone, holds the conversation, and decides whether the booking changes. No message goes to an employee on its own.
data_needed: The booking and its attachments
The exception that triggered the check
The site and the role of the person who entered it, used only for this check
The CAO or VAT rule the booking is being tested against
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint close or audit file, stating the booking, the fact found and the correction. The note does not score the employee.

evidence.claim: Audit sampling and exception lists from a ledger export are standard functions in CaseWare IDEA.
A conversation about how a warehouse booking was made still needs a person the employee can talk to.
A tool that selects or assesses named employees can require works-council consent under the WOR and can fall in the EU AI Act's high-risk category for worker management.

risks: An automatic message to a warehouse employee about a wrong booking damages trust and can become a staff-monitoring matter for the works council.
Employee names and interview notes sent to a general model can breach the AVG. The check should run on the booking, with names kept in AFAS and SharePoint.
A question list written as if fraud were already found will turn a cutoff error into a conflict on the floor.
research_questions: What share of current samples is answered by the attachment alone, with no conversation?
Who do the accountants speak to today: bookkeepers, site clerks, or both, and how long does it take to reach shift staff?
Has the works council already been consulted on tools that select individual bookings or named staff?
How often does a conversation change the booking, and how often does it only explain it?

role.altitude: The accountant stops rebuilding the pack, the VAT bridge, the lease schedules and the lead sheets, and owns the close design: the checks, the mapping, the rate and VAT rules, and the exceptions that still need a person.
reach: Bookkeeper: clear VAT codes and subledger breaks on agency and carrier invoices before they reach the return.
FP&A analyst: write the first bridge from locked actuals to the forecast the sites are asked to trust.
Controller: keep the control catalogue and the first draft of the management-letter reply.
Payroll specialist: tie holiday pay, shift premiums and the wage accrual under both CAOs back to the general ledger.
Credit and collections officer: explain the debtor movement in the monthly pack from the same ledger that drives days sales outstanding.
role.ceiling_note: Two accountants cannot also clear the bookkeepers' invoice volume or run the FP&A cycle. Close speed stays capped by late agency invoices, the Rabobank cut-off and the nightly AFAS extract. Filing with the Belastingdienst, the board's adoption of the jaarrekening and the replies to the external auditor stay named people's work. Works-council consent and the AVG limit any check that uses named employee data.
skills_to_grow: The AFAS data model: VAT codes, site cost centres, and how subledgers tie to the general ledger
Dutch GAAP for leases, accruals and the jaarrekening, plus VAT on transport and warehouse services
Writing a check so a wrong balance fails before the pack is sent
Reading an assisted draft against the ledger and rejecting commentary the figures do not support
Enough Power BI or SQL to see why a nightly figure moved
role.ambitious_version: A close the site leads trust by working day four: each site's result, the flex-labour bridge and the forecast variance, with VAT and the balance sheet already tied. The two accountants spend the month on leases, lane margin and the control gaps, and the audit-adjustment list is short because the breaks were fixed in the month they happened.
